questions.stem: A lakehouse reads data from Amazon S3 through shortcuts, and the cloud provider charges for every read out of S3. Which workspace setting can reduce those charges?

options.text: High concurrency mode
Shortcut caching for the workspace
V-Order
The workspace's default environment

questions.explanation: With shortcut caching on (a OneLake setting in the workspace settings), files read through Amazon S3, S3-compatible, Google Cloud Storage and on-premises gateway shortcuts are kept in OneLake for a retention period of 1 to 28 days, so repeat reads don't go back to the source.

questions.stem: A shortcut cache is turned on for a workspace. What happens to a cached file that nobody reads for longer than the retention period you set?

options.text: It is deleted from the cache and from the source storage account as well
It is removed from the cache, and the next read fetches it from the source again
The shortcut stops resolving until someone resets the workspace's cache
It stays in the cache permanently, since retention applies only to newly cached files

questions.explanation: Each access resets the retention period. A file not read within it is purged from the cache, and the next read goes to the source and caches it again. The source is never changed.

questions.stem: A tool outside Fabric needs to read a lakehouse's files through the ADLS Gen2 API. Which address form does OneLake use?

options.text: `sql://<workspace>.onelake.fabric.microsoft.com/<item>.Lakehouse/Files/...`
`abfss://<workspace>@onelake.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com/<item>.Lakehouse/Files/...`
`file://onelake.fabric.microsoft.com/<workspace>/<item>.Lakehouse/Files/<folder>/...`
`https://<workspace>.blob.core.windows.net/<item>.Lakehouse/Files/...`

questions.explanation: OneLake supports the ADLS Gen2 APIs, with the workspace as the container and the item, with its type, as the top folder.

questions.stem: A user deletes a file from a lakehouse by mistake. What does OneLake offer to get it back?

options.text: Nothing: deletes in OneLake are immediate and final
Soft delete: deleted files are kept for a period and can be restored
The file can be restored only through Git
A nightly backup that only Microsoft Support can restore

questions.explanation: OneLake soft delete keeps deleted files for seven days. You can restore them with Azure Storage Explorer, Azure PowerShell or the Azure Storage REST APIs if you have write access to the files.

questions.stem: Shortcut caching is on for a workspace with S3 shortcuts. Repeat reads of one 3 GB Parquet file still go out to S3. Why?

options.text: Caching only applies after the workspace is assigned to a domain
The retention period is shorter than one day
Caching only works for files in the Tables folder
Individual files greater than 1 GB aren't cached

questions.explanation: Shortcut caching skips individual files larger than 1 GB, so they're always read from the source.

questions.stem: After a source system reloaded its files in Google Cloud Storage, you want every cached copy in the workspace thrown away at once. What do you do?

options.text: Delete and recreate each shortcut so its cached files are rebuilt
Lower the retention period to one day and wait for the purge to run
Select Reset cache in the OneLake tab of the workspace settings
Turn on soft delete for the lakehouse

questions.explanation: Reset cache removes all files from the workspace's shortcut cache immediately. Lowering the retention period only purges files over time.

questions.stem: A workspace turns on shortcut caching. Which two shortcut sources can have their files cached? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Dataverse
Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2
Google Cloud Storage
A lakehouse in another Fabric workspace
Amazon S3

questions.explanation: Shortcut caching supports Google Cloud Storage, S3, S3 compatible and on-premises data gateway shortcuts. ADLS Gen2, internal OneLake and Dataverse shortcuts aren't in the list.

questions.stem: No one in your organization can start the OneLake file explorer app. Which setting is most likely turned off?

options.text: The Users can sync data in OneLake with the OneLake File Explorer app tenant setting
The workspace's shortcut caching setting in the OneLake tab of each workspace's settings
The default domain assigned to the user's security group in the admin portal
High concurrency mode for notebooks in the workspace's Spark compute settings

questions.explanation: When that tenant setting is off, the app can't start for anyone in the organization. The other settings don't control the app.

questions.stem: A pipeline wrote new files to a lakehouse folder. A user who browses the folder in OneLake file explorer doesn't see them. What should the user do?

options.text: Right-click the folder and select OneLake > Sync from OneLake
Ask a workspace admin to reset the shortcut cache
Wait for the nightly full download
Reinstall OneLake file explorer

questions.explanation: Changes made outside File Explorer aren't synced automatically. Sync from OneLake pulls the latest files and folders.

questions.stem: A lakehouse has a shortcut to a folder in another lakehouse. An engineer deletes the shortcut itself. What happens to the data in the target folder?

options.text: It is moved to the lakehouse's recycle bin for seven days
It is deleted too, because shortcuts cascade deletes to the target
It stays unchanged; only the shortcut object is deleted
It becomes read-only until a new shortcut is created

questions.explanation: Shortcuts don't cascade deletes. Deleting the shortcut removes only the shortcut, though deleting a file inside a shortcut does delete it in the target if you have permission there.
